rationale: Developmental delay and intellectual disability (DD/ID) are consistently reported across virtually all individuals with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS) due to PSMD12 haploinsufficiency across multiple series (Ebstein et al. 2023, Feresin et al. 2025, Isidor et al. 2022). However, the specific claim that 'severe expressive speech impairment occurs in essentially 100% of reported individuals' is conflicted. OMIM #617516 explicitly records sub-cohorts where speech delay was noted in only a subset (e.g. 3 individuals), and while prevalent speech delay is a recognized hallmark, expressivity is described as highly variable across clinical cohorts.

evidence.text: All affected individuals with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome caused by PSMD12 truncating variants were documented to present with developmental delay.

source.title: PSMC3 proteasome subunit variants are associated with neurodevelopmental delay and type I interferon production
source.quote: all affected children exhibited developmental delay (DD)

evidence.text: In a family study of six patients (four adults) with inherited truncating PSMD12 variants, all individuals presented with developmental delay and intellectual disability, with global developmental delay and prevalent speech delay noted.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating PSMD12 Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Portraying a completely penetrant condition with inter- and intra-familiar clinical variability, all individuals presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies.

evidence.text: A clinical expansion study of 24 additional unrelated patients with STISS observed that the expressivity of most clinical features is highly variable, though DD/ID and speech delay were consistently prominent.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: The expressivity of most clinical features in STISS is highly variable. In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome.

evidence.text: OMIM entry for Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome records developmental delay with intellectual disability across patients, but specifically notes motor delay in two patients and speech delay in three patients within a cited sub-group, conflicting with a universal 100% presentation of severe speech delay.

source.title: 617516 - STANKIEWICZ-ISIDOR SYNDROME; STISS
source.quote: The patients had developmental delay with intellectual disability and abnormal behavior, including autism. Two patients had motor delay and 3 had speech delay.

conflicts: While DD/ID appears completely penetrant (approaching 100%), the presence and severity of expressive speech impairment varies; OMIM documentation highlights cohorts where only a subset had speech delay explicitly recorded rather than 100% severe expressive impairment.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and spectrum of expressive speech delay versus receptive language preservation across all pooled PSMD12 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic cross-cohort phenotyping using standardized speech and language assessments is required to determine whether speech impairment is an invariable cardinal sign or variable in expressivity.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-truncating or inherited PSMD12 variants produce milder speech phenotypes compared to de novo truncating variants?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in clinical severity between familial inherited variants and de novo loss-of-function variants could account for phenotypic variations in speech and cognitive outcomes.
